question: to the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Lefteris Nikolaou-Alavanos (NI) Subject:

The long-suffering people of Palestine face all kinds of deprivation and bloody raids by the Israeli military. The misleadingly named ‘Peace Council’ lays the foundations for ‘rebuilding’ Gaza on the basis of the toxic plan America has announced for Gaza and the West Bank. The ‘International Stabilisation Force’ is to be set up in Gaza , turning it into an American-Israeli protectorate. By participating as an ‘observer’, Nea Dimokratia bears a great deal of responsibility for this. The EU and Member States bear the same responsibility as they are following the same policy. The Palestinian people are essentially living through the ceasefire with a gun pointed at their heads because of the criminal policy pursued by Israel and its allies. In view of the above, can the Vice-President/High Representative answer the following: 1.

What is its position regarding the fact that with the US and Israel’s plans to expand the war into the Middle East and Israel's continued pursuit of its criminal policy, despite the ceasefire, the Palestinians face bloody raids, illegal settlements and inhumane deprivations, without access to basic necessities?

What is its position regarding the so-called ‘International Stabilisation Force’ and the misleadingly named ‘Peace Council’, which imposes US and Israeli plans to ‘rebuild’ Gaza by displacing Palestinians and confiscating their property, promoting the interests of business groups in the countries responsible for the genocide, the displacement of the Palestinian people and support for these criminal plans?

What is its position regarding the call for the establishment of an independent Palestinian state based on the 1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital, territorial unity without settlements and foreign troops, and with the right of refugees to return from all the structures and the grip of power of the other states?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.4.2026) The EU has been deeply concerned about the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza. The EU has called on the Israeli authorities, including on humanitarian access, dual-use policy and international non-governmental registration, to address the enormous needs of the population. The EU is totally opposed to forced displacement of the Palestinian population or to geographical or demographic changes in Gaza. The EU strongly condemns the ongoing extremist settler violence in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, and recalls that Israel has the duty to protect civilians and hold perpetrators accountable. The EU is not a member of the Board of Peace and its participation as an observer at the inaugural meeting of the Board of Peace in Washington, District of Columbia, focused on Gaza’s reconstruction, is to be seen as part of the EU’s commitment to the implementation of the ceasefire in Gaza and international efforts for recovery and reconstruction. The EU welcomed the adoption of UN Security Council (UNSC) Resolution 2803 and stands ready to work together with the US on the implementation of the comprehensive Peace Plan for Gaza. The EU has an important role to play in this context, being the biggest provider of external assistance to the Palestinians, including EUR 124 million in humanitarian aid confirmed for 20261. The EU is committed to lasting and sustainable peace in accordance with the relevant UNSC resolutions, on the basis of the two-state solution, with the State of Israel and an independent, democratic, contiguous, sovereign and viable State of Palestine living side-by-side in peace, security and mutual recognition, and Jerusalem serving as the future capital of both states. The EU supports the diplomatic efforts anchored in international law.
